mappings.note: Simplifying 12:36 is bare ratio work. LO-99 is per cent and LO-100 is direct/inverse proportion problems; neither reaches a ratio on its own, so the competency that names proportional reasoning in commercial situations is cited.
Ratio of 10 m to 10 km needs a unit conversion first, but is still bare ratio -> competency, same gap as above.
Converting the ratio 3:4 to a percentage is the per cent concept itself -> LO-99, not the ratio-only competency.
2:5 expressed as a percentage -> LO-99.
50 per cent of 20 students; straight per cent of a quantity -> LO-99.
20 per cent increase on Rs 34,000 -> LO-99's per cent application, the increase case rather than discount.
Discount per cent from marked price 840 and selling price 714; LO-99 names this case explicitly.
10 per cent salary increase -> LO-99.
Selling price at 15 per cent profit on cost plus overheads -> LO-99's profit and loss case.
Price before a 10 per cent tax from the tax-inclusive Rs 3300 -> LO-99's VAT case, worked backwards.
Selling price after an 8 per cent discount on a marked price of 2000 -> LO-99 discount case.
Cost price from a selling price of 210 at a 10 per cent loss -> LO-99 profit and loss, worked backwards.
5 km/h against 500 m/h is a unit-conversion ratio with no per cent and no proportion problem -> competency.
The text layer flattened 3/5 to '35'; the item converts that fraction to a percentage -> LO-99. Flattening flagged.
25 per cent of 60 students -> LO-99.
What VAT is computed on; LO-99 names VAT specifically, so this is the outcome rather than the competency.
Selling price after a 25 per cent discount on Rs 200 -> LO-99.

Simple interest on Rs 4000 for 2 years at 8 per cent. LO-99 names compound interest but not simple interest; it is the same per-cent-of-a-principal application and is the only outcome that reaches interest at all, so LO-99 with that gap noted.
Time for Rs 1600 to compound to Rs 1764 at 5 per cent -> LO-99's compound interest case, solved for the period.

Dividing Rs 782 into parts proportional to 1/2 : 2/3 : 3/4 is direct proportion applied to sharing -> LO-100, not the bare-ratio competency used for the simplification items, because a proportion is being solved.
Principal from a given simple interest, rate and time -> LO-99, with the simple-interest gap noted as for qid:113657.
Quarterly compounding adjusts the rate to r/4 -> LO-99's compound interest case.
Compound interest payable half-yearly on Rs 4000 -> LO-99.
Profit and loss per cent is computed on cost price; a base-of-the-percentage item -> LO-99.
Discount is computed on marked price; the companion base item -> LO-99.
Cost price plus profit gives selling price; the relation LO-99's profit and loss work rests on.
Definition of a ratio as comparison by division. Definitional and about ratio rather than per cent or a proportion problem, so the competency.
New salary ratio after 15, 10 and 20 per cent increments; the ratio is only the vehicle, the assessed step is the per cent increase -> LO-99.
30 per cent of 100 students -> LO-99.
Solving 0.75 : x :: 5 : 8 is a direct proportion equation -> LO-100, not the bare-ratio competency.
Rate of a simple interest bond from two amounts at different times -> LO-99, with the same simple-interest gap noted.
Which formula gives the amount under half-yearly compounding -> LO-99's compound interest case.
Ratio 5:4 expressed as a per cent -> LO-99, as with the other ratio-to-percentage items.
Rent for four months from a yearly rent varies directly with time -> LO-100. No per cent is involved, so not LO-99.
25 per cent of 40 students (same item as qid:113654 with a different total) -> LO-99.
